'''Michele 'Miki' De Palma''' (born 1973, [[Italy]]) is an Italian biologist and a professor at [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|EPFL (École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne)]]. He is known for his work on the role of [[macrophage]]s in cancer progression and the discovery of [[TEK tyrosine kinase|Tie2]]-expressing [[Angiogenesis|angiogenic]] [[monocyte]]s.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Michele De Palma|url=https://people.epfl.ch/michele.depalma?lang=en|access-date=2020-09-10|website=people.epfl.ch}}</ref>

== Career ==
De Palma obtained a master's degree in biology from the [[University of Turin]] in 1999 after defending his thesis on the [[Cytostasis|cytostatic]] effects of [[Interferon type I|type-I interferons]] on [[cancer cell]]s. He then obtained a PhD in 2004 in the laboratory of Luigi Naldini, where he studied the effect of bone marrow-derived cells on tumor [[angiogenesis]], and performed postdoctoral work at the Telethon Institute for Gene Therapy in [[Milan]], further dissecting the role of [[macrophage]]s and their potential use as a target for [[gene therapy]] in the [[treatment of cancer]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Michele De Palma {{!}} VIB Conferences|url=https://www.vibconferences.be/speaker/michele-de-palma|access-date=2020-09-10|website=www.vibconferences.be|language=en}}</ref>

De Palma was appointed group leader at the San Raffaele Scientific Institute in 2008. In 2012, he was named tenure-track assistant professor at [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|EPFL]], where he was promoted to associate professor in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|title=15 new professors appointed at the two Federal Institutes of Technology|url=https://www.seco.admin.ch/seco/en/home/seco/nsb-news.msg-id-71504.html|access-date=2020-09-10|website=www.seco.admin.ch}}</ref>

== Research ==
De Palma heads the Angiogenesis and Tumor Microenvironment group at [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|EPFL]]. His research focuses on the influence of the [[tumor microenvironment]] on cancer progression.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Research Activities|url=https://www.epfl.ch/labs/depalma-lab/research/|access-date=2020-09-10|website=www.epfl.ch|language=en-GB}}</ref> De Palma and colleagues use genetic models of cancer as well as [[Genetic engineering|genetically engineered]] cells to decipher the complex interactions occurring between tumor cells, [[blood vessel]]s, [[White blood cell|immune cells]] and [[Exosome (vesicle)|exosomes]] in the [[tumor microenvironment]].

De Palma is known for having discovered a subpopulation of [[TEK tyrosine kinase|Tie2]]-positive [[monocyte]]s endowed with [[Angiogenesis|angiogenic]] capabilities, and which elicit tumor progression.<ref>{{Cite journal|date=2005-09-01|title=Tie2 identifies a hematopoietic lineage of proangiogenic monocytes required for tumor vessel formation and a mesenchymal population of pericyte progenitors|journal=Cancer Cell|language=en|volume=8|issue=3|pages=211–226|doi=10.1016/j.ccr.2005.08.002|issn=1535-6108|last1=De Palma|first1=Michele|last2=Venneri|first2=Mary later showed that inhibition of the [[TEK tyrosine kinase|Tie2]]-ligand [[ANGPT2|Angiopoietin 2]] induces tumor regression and inhibits [[metastasis]] by preventing [[angiogenesis]].<ref>{{Cite The laboratory of De Palma explores novel therapeutic strategies to overcome resistance to [[Cancer immunotherapy|cancer immunotherapies]]. De Palma and colleagues notably showed that dual inhibition of [[TEK tyrosine kinase|Tie2]] and [[Vascular endothelial growth factor A|VEGF-A]] promotes anti-tumor immunity and potentiates treatment by [[immune checkpoint]] inhibitors.<ref>{{Cite De Palma and colleagues also explore the role of [[extracellular vesicle]]s in cancer progression and resistance to therapy. In 2019, they showed that [[chemotherapy]] stimulates the release of tumor-derivered pro-metastatic [[Exosome (vesicle)|exosomes]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Keklikoglou|first1=Ioanna|last2=Cianciaruso|first2=Chiara|last3=Güç|first3=Esra|last4=Squadrito|first4=Mario Leonardo|last5=Spring|first5=Laura M.|last6=Tazzyman|first6=Simon|last7=Lambein|first7=Lore|last8=Poissonnier|first8=Amanda|last9=Ferraro|first9=Gino B.|last10=Baer|first10=Caroline|last11=Cassará|first11=Antonino|date=February 2019|title=Chemotherapy elicits pro-metastatic extracellular vesicles in breast cancer models|journal=Nature Cell Biology|language=en|volume=21|issue=2|pages=190–202|doi=10.1038/s41556-018-0256-3|pmid=30598531|pmc=6525097|issn=1476-4679}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Exosomes Linked to Cancer Spread from Chemoresistant Tumors in Mice|url=https://www.the-scientist.com/news-opinion/exosomes-linked-to-cancer-spread-from-chemoresistant-tumors-in-mice-65306|access-date=2020-09-15|website=The Scientist Magazine®|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Tumors backfire on chemotherapy|url=https://www.eurekalert.org/pub_releases/2018-12/epfd-tbo122618.php|access-date=2020-09-15|website=EurekAlert!|language=en}}</ref> De Palma's group also developed a new generation of [[cancer vaccine]] based on [[dendritic cell]]s engineered with a chimeric receptor called ''EVIR'', designed to internalize tumor-derived [[Exosome (vesicle)|exosomes]] and associated [[Tumor antigen|cancer antigens]], thus stimulating anti-tumor immunity.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Squadrito|first1=Mario Leonardo|last2=Cianciaruso|first2=Chiara|last3=Hansen|first3=Sarah K.|last4=De Palma|first4=Michele|date=March 2018|title=EVIR: chimeric receptors that enhance dendritic cell cross-dressing with tumor antigens|journal=Nature Methods|language=en|volume=15|issue=3|pages=183–186|doi=10.1038/nmeth.4579|pmid=29355847|pmc=5833950|issn=1548-7105}}</ref>

De Palma has also published multiple studies on the [[Taxonomy (biology)|taxonomy]] of [[scarabaeidae]], including the description of several new species.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=De Palma|first1=Michele|last2=Takano|first2=Hitoshi|last3=Léonard|first3=Philippe|last4=Bouyer|first4=Thierry|date=2020|title=Barcoding analysis and taxonomic revision of Goliathus Lamarck, 1802 (Scarabaeidae, Cetoniinae)|url=http://www.entomoafricana.org/ent%20afr%202020%2025%201%20De%20palma%20et%20al%20goliathus%20b.pdf|journal=Entemologia Africana|volume=25|issue=1|pages=11–32}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Data scaraebaeoidea Bibliography|url=http://www.datascaraebaeoidea.net/Referenties/D.html|access-date=16 September 2020}}</ref>

== Distinctions ==
In 2013, De Palma was awarded with the Leenaards Scientific Prize for his research on anti-angiogenic therapies and cancer immunotherapy.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Cibler l'angiogenèse et les réseaux immunosuppresseurs pour améliorer le traitement des cancers du sein et de l'ovaire|url=https://www.leenaards.ch/prix/cibler-langiogenese-et-les-reseaux-immunosuppresseurs-pour-ameliorer-le-traitement-des-cancers-du-sein-et-de-lovaire/|access-date=2020-09-15|website=Fondation Leenaards - Favoriser la dynamique créatrice|language=fr}}</ref> He also received the Robert Wenner Prize in 2017, presented by the Swiss Cancer League.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Lauréats du Prix Robert Wenner depuis 1983|url=https://www.liguecancer.ch/la-recherche/recompenses/prix-robert-wenner/-dl-/fileadmin/downloads/forschung/prix-robert-wenner-laureats-depuis-1983.pdf|language=fr}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Papageorgiou|first=Nik|title=Michele De Palma wins 2017 Swiss Cancer League prize|url=https://actu.epfl.ch/news/michele-de-palma-wins-2017-swiss-cancer-league-p-2/|access-date=15 September 2020|website=epfl.ch|date=30 November 2017 }}</ref>

De Palma received a starting grant in 2009 and a consolidator grant in 2016 from the [[European Research Council]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=ERC FUNDED PROJECTS|url=https://erc.europa.eu/projects-figures/erc-funded-projects/results|access-date=2020-09-15|website=ERC: European Research Council|language=en}}</ref>

De Palma serves on the scientific advisory and editorial board of several [[Peer review|peer-reviewed]] scientific journals, such as ''[[Science Translational Medicine]]'',<ref>{{Cite web|title=Editorial staff and scientific advisory boards {{!}} Science Translational Medicine|url=https://stm.sciencemag.org/content/editorial-staff-and-scientific-advisory-boards|access-date=2020-09-15|website=stm.sciencemag.org}}</ref> ''[[Cell Reports]]'',<ref>{{Cite web|title=Cell Press: Cell Reports|url=https://www.cell.com/cell-reports/advisory-board|access-date=2020-09-15|website=www.cell.com}}</ref> [[BBA - Reviews on Cancer|''BBA Reviews on Cancer'']]<ref>{{Cite web|title=Editorial board - Biochimica et Biophysica Acta (BBA) - Reviews on Cancer {{!}} ScienceDirect.com by Elsevier|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/biochimica-et-biophysica-acta-bba-reviews-on-cancer/about/editorial-board|access-date=2020-09-15|website=www.sciencedirect.com}}</ref> and ''Cancer Immunology Research.''<ref>{{Cite web|title=Editorial Board {{!}} Cancer Immunology Research|url=https://cancerimmunolres.aacrjournals.org/about|access-date=2020-09-15|website=cancerimmunolres.aacrjournals.org}}</ref>
